title: ai-atoms bundle v1
description: A bundle atom — a multi-file skill that does not fit in a single system-prompt fragment: agent personas, templates, contracts, docs, and/or a runtime module shipped together as one self-contained unit. Every file is inlined; a bundle never references content that is not shipped inside the atom.

id.description: Namespaced identifier in the form bundle/<slug>.

version.description: Semantic version of this bundle atom.

description.description: What this bundle does, when to invoke it, and what it prevents.

entry_point.description: Path, relative to the bundle root, of the primary document a consumer should read/execute first (e.g. "SKILL.md"). Must match the `path` of one entry in `files`.

files.description: Every file shipped inside this bundle, fully inlined. A bundle must never reference a file it does not ship here.

path.description: Relative path from the bundle root, forward-slash separated. No leading slash, no `..` segments.

role.description: What this file is for: entry = primary document, agent = a subagent/persona definition, contract = a machine-checked schema/interface, template = text a caller fills in and dispatches, doc = human-facing narrative documentation, runtime = executable implementation code, config = declarative configuration (permissions, graphs, etc.).

applicable_domains.description: Domains where this bundle applies (e.g. code, design, planning, debug, agents).

depends_on.description: Other bundle or skill atoms this one depends on or installs alongside.

invocation.description: Slash-command invocation forms, e.g. ["/develop", "/develop clean"]. Omit for bundles with no slash-command entry point.

authored_by.description: Key atom ID or author identifier (e.g. 'convergent-systems-key', 'anthropics', 'kepano').

source_url.description: URL of the original source file when this atom was imported from an external open-source repository. Used for attribution and tracking upstream changes.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle stage of this bundle atom.
